title: SCIM lifecycle: deferred deprovision and out-of-order update repair playbook
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: Multiple customers and internal audits surfaced scenarios where SCIM-driven deprovisioning and group updates resulted in partial state (user removed from some groups but not others) or transient re-provisioning due to race conditions across our async workers. These cases increase risk (stale access) and trigger support tickets.

Problem: The current SCIM pipeline retries are simple exponential backoff without coordinated tombstones or deferred finalization windows. When downstream identity providers or internal store outages occur, retries + eventual consistency can cause out-of-order operations (e.g., group removal processed before a later group add), leading to orphaned membership, duplicate provisions, or accidental re-enables after admin-initiated deprovision.

Goal: Implement a robust deferred-deprovision + repair playbook that provides safe, observable SCIM semantics: 1) a short grace/deferred-finalization window for deprovision, 2) tombstone markers and idempotent operation keys to prevent accidental re-provision, 3) a reconciliation/repair job for partial updates, and 4) auditable trails surfaced to Console and incident pages.

Proposed design (high level):
- Deferred deprovision: convert immediate user disable -> "pending_deprovision" state for a configurable grace period (default 24h) when triggered via SCIM deprovision. During pending window, block sign-in and API tokens while keeping account metadata for rollback.
- Tombstone & operation tokens: emit a tombstone record with operation_id for each user/group deprovision. All downstream retry logic must include operation_id to ensure idempotency and allow "ignore if tombstoned" semantics.
- Ordered operation sequencing: attach logical sequence numbers per resource (user/group) and enforce apply-if-seq >= current to mitigate out-of-order native processing when workers replay messages.
- Repair/reconciliation job: periodic, strongly-consistent job that scans for partial-state indicators (mismatched group memberships, disabled-but-active sessions), cross-checks SCIM source-of-truth, and emits corrective operations or alerts depending on confidence level.
- Dead-letter queue and escalation: non-idempotent failures or repeated divergent states move to DLQ with automatic ticket creation and an "admin repair" workflow in Console for safe manual intervention.
- Audit logging & Console surfaces: every SCIM action (incoming request, internal state transition, retry, tombstone creation, reconciliation correction) must be logged with actor, op_id, seq, reason, and correlated trace_id. Expose a per-user SCIM timeline in Console with links to raw logs and the reconciliation run that touched the resource.
- Backwards compatibility: default behavior mirrors current immediate-deprovision for orgs who opt-out; provide org-level toggles and migration path.

Implementation notes:
- Runtime changes: extend identity service schema to include state, tombstone_at, last_seq, last_op_id. Use compact string fields to remain compatible with storage constraints.
- Worker changes: include op_id and seq validation in the SCIM processor; make retries include the original op_id header. On tombstoned resources, workers should return 200/OK for idempotent replays but record an audit event.
- Reconciliation: implement an eventual-scan lambda (or k8s job) that runs hourly for high-activity tenants and daily for low-activity. Use sampling/priority to avoid scanning very large orgs too frequently.
- Metrics & alerts: add counters for partial-state detections, tombstone creations, DLQ entries, reconciliation corrections, and mean time to repair (MTTR). Create an SLO to keep partial-state rate <0.05% of SCIM ops for tiered orgs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deferred-deprovision state implemented and togglable per-org; unit + integration tests cover state transitions.
- Tombstone/op_id flow enforced across worker pool; retries with same op_id are idempotent and recorded as "replay".
- Reconciliation job detects and corrects at least two representative partial-state scenarios in staging with telemetry proving correction.
- Console shows per-user SCIM timeline with links to the reconciliation run and raw audit lines.
- New metrics and dashboards created; alerts fire on DLQ growth and reconciliation failure rates.
- Security review completed and documented in PRD; feature gated behind rollout flag.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature branch + unit tests; add schema migrations behind flags.
2) Deploy worker changes to staging; run reconciliation in dry-run mode against staging orgs.
3) Canary rollout to <5 small orgs with enabled toggle; monitor DLQ and partial-state metrics for 72h.
4) Gradual expansion with options for customer opt-in and a migration tool to backfill tombstones for past deprovisions.

Notes and tradeoffs:
- Deferred deprovision increases time-to-finalize deprovision for admins; mitigated by immediate token revocation and sign-in block.
- Reconciliation adds compute cost; we tune cadence per-org size and run aggressive repairs only when confidence is high.
- Some legacy SCIM connectors expect immediate removal; provide compatibility mode and a migration doc for customer admins.
comments: 2025-03-01: Triage - Customer-facing ticket opened by Support referencing multiple orgs reporting stale access after SCIM deprovision. Assigned to Marcus.
2025-03-03: Design review with PM/Product - agreed on deferred finalization + tombstones; PM asked for Console timeline mockups.
2025-03-05: Engineering spike - validated seq-based guard works on local worker pool; found race when op_id not propagated through retry envelope.
2025-03-07: PR created - https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8142 (worker changes + schema migration behind feature flag).
2025-03-10: Security review requested - submitted threat model and audit plan. Noted KMS access pattern for audit log signing.
2025-03-12: Running reconciliation dry-run in staging - detected 12 partial-state cases across staging tenants; dry-run proposed corrections match operator expectations.

Action items:
- Add manual 'force finalize' button in Console for admins (UX task: DES-22345).
- Coordinate migration doc with Docs and Solutions (owner: Marcus).
- Wire up DLQ -> ticket automation (follow-up ENG-86077).
